subaward_description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AGREEMENT IS TO CATALYZE CUTTING-EDGE, TECHNOLOGY-DRIVEN TRANSFORMATION IN RURAL HEAL CARE DELIVERY BY BLENDING PUBLIC NEBRASKA’S RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) FUNDING WITH PRIVATE INVESTMENT. OHIO'S RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT INITIATIVES TO IMPROVE HEALTH FOR RURAL OHIOANS THROUGH INNOVATION, HEALTHCARE ACCESS, AND PREVENTION. - THE OHIO RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) PRESENTS THIS PLAN TO STRENGTHEN HEALTHCARE ACCESS, OUTCOMES, AND WORKFORCE CAPACITY ACROSS OHIO’S 73 NON-URBAN COUNTIES. THE 4.4 MILLION RESIDENTS LIVING IN THESE RURAL COMMUNITIES ARE IMPACTED BY LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE, HOSPITAL CLOSURES, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND HIGH RATES OF CHRONIC AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. RURAL AND APPALACHIAN OHIOANS EXPERIENCE HIGHER RATES OF HEART DISEASE, DIABETES, COPD, CANCER, AND SUICIDE THAN STATE AVERAGES. THIRTEEN COUNTIES ARE MATERNITY CARE DESERTS, AND NEARLY ONE IN FIVE RURAL HOSPITALS IS AT RISK OF CLOSURE. PROVIDER SHORTAGES ARE WIDESPREAD: PRIMARY CARE AVAILABILITY IS NEARLY HALF THAT OF URBAN REGIONS, AND BEHAVIORAL AND ORAL HEALTH GAPS PERSIST. THESE CHALLENGES ARE COMPOUNDED BY LOWER EDUCATION LEVELS, HIGHER POVERTY, AND AN AGING POPULATION—ONE IN THREE RURAL OHIOANS IS OVER AGE 60. OHIO’S PLAN ALIGNS WITH FEDERAL PRIORITIES TO MAKE RURAL AMERICA HEALTHY AGAIN THROUGH SUSTAINABLE ACCESS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, INNOVATIVE CARE, AND TECH ADVANCEMENT. KEY INITIATIVES: RURAL HEALTH INNOVATION HUBS – ESTABLISH CLINICALLY INTEGRATED NETWORKS (CINS) AND REGIONAL CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE LINKING HOSPITALS, CLINICS, EMS, PHARMACISTS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO COORDINATE CARE, REDUCE COSTS, AND EXPAND CAPACITY. LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ALLOW LOW-RISK BIRTHING CENTERS IN RURAL HOSPITALS. EMERGENCY CARE TRANSFORMATION – SCALE A SUCCESSFUL PILOT ENABLING EMS TO PROVIDE TREAT-IN-PLACE OR ALTERNATE-DESTINATION CARE, REDUCING UNNECESSARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT USE THROUGH TRAINING, SYSTEM UPGRADES, AND IMPROVED CONNECTIVITY. SCHOOL-BASED HEALTH CENTERS – ESTABLISH CLINICS ON K–12 AND COLLEGE CAMPUSES OFFERING PRIMARY, BEHAVIORAL, DENTAL, AND TELEHEALTH SERVICES FOR STUDENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS, SERVING ALSO AS RURAL CLINICAL TRAINING SITES. OH SEE – EXPAND STATEWIDE MOBILE VISION, HEARING, AND DENTAL CARE BASED ON A 13-COUNTY PILOT TO ENSURE EARLY DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN. RURAL WORKFORCE PIPELINE – BUILD A CONTINUUM FROM HIGH SCHOOL THROUGH PROFESSIONAL TRAINING AND EMPLOYMENT, FEATURING UPSKILLING FOR COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS AND PHARMACISTS, FIVE-YEAR RURAL SERVICE COMMITMENTS, AND PARTNERSHIPS AMONG SCHOOLS, UNIVERSITIES, AND EMPLOYERS. CROSS-CUTTING STRATEGIES: RHTP EMBEDS TELEHEALTH, REMOTE MONITORING, AND INTEROPERABLE ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS ACROSS INITIATIVES. POLICY ACTIONS INCLUDE EXPANDING PHARMACIST SCOPE OF PRACTICE, ESTABLISHING RURAL BIRTHING CENTERS, REINSTATING THE PRESIDENTIAL FITNESS TEST, AND REQUIRING PHYSICIAN NUTRITION CME. MORE THAN 300 PARTNERS (HOSPITALS, FQHCS, UNIVERSITIES, EMS, ASSOCIATIONS) COLLABORATED ON THE PLAN. IMPLEMENTATION WILL OCCUR THROUGH LOCAL PARTNERS WITH STATE OVERSIGHT. SUSTAINABILITY: EACH PROJECT IS DESIGNED FOR LONG-TERM VIABILITY THROUGH BILLABLE SERVICE MODELS, SHARED-SERVICE EFFICIENCIES, AND ALIGNMENT WITH MEDICAID AND VALUE-BASED PAYMENT SYSTEMS. WORKFORCE INCENTIVES, TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION, AND LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ENSURE CONTINUITY BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD. EXPECTED OUTCOMES BY 2031: • ESTABLISH REGIONAL INTEGRATED NETWORKS ACROSS ALL RURAL COUNTIES. EXPANDED RURAL SBHCS. • REDUCE AVOIDABLE EMERGENCY VISITS THROUGH EMS INNOVATION. • IMPROVE DIABETES AND HYPERTENSION OUTCOMES STATEWIDE. • INCREASE THE RURAL HEALTH WORKFORCE BY AT LEAST 20%. • STRENGTHEN MATERNAL, BEHAVIORAL, AND PREVENTIVE CARE ACCESS. CONCLUSION: THIS REPRESENTS A BOLD, DATA-DRIVEN TRANSFORMATION OF RURAL HEALTHCARE IN OHIO. THROUGH TECHNOLOGY, POLICY INNOVATION, AND CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION, THE PROGRAM WILL CREATE A SUSTAINABLE MODEL THAT IMPROVES CARE QUALITY, STRENGTHENS THE WORKFORCE, AND ENHANCES HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR RURAL OHIOANS.

OHIO'S RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT INITIATIVES TO IMPROVE HEALTH FOR RURAL OHIOANS THROUGH INNOVATION, HEALTHCARE ACCESS, AND PREVENTION. - THE OHIO RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) PRESENTS THIS PLAN TO STRENGTHEN HEALTHCARE ACCESS, OUTCOMES, AND WORKFORCE CAPACITY ACROSS OHIO’S 73 NON-URBAN COUNTIES. THE 4.4 MILLION RESIDENTS LIVING IN THESE RURAL COMMUNITIES ARE IMPACTED BY LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE, HOSPITAL CLOSURES, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND HIGH RATES OF CHRONIC AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. RURAL AND APPALACHIAN OHIOANS EXPERIENCE HIGHER RATES OF HEART DISEASE, DIABETES, COPD, CANCER, AND SUICIDE THAN STATE AVERAGES. THIRTEEN COUNTIES ARE MATERNITY CARE DESERTS, AND NEARLY ONE IN FIVE RURAL HOSPITALS IS AT RISK OF CLOSURE. PROVIDER SHORTAGES ARE WIDESPREAD: PRIMARY CARE AVAILABILITY IS NEARLY HALF THAT OF URBAN REGIONS, AND BEHAVIORAL AND ORAL HEALTH GAPS PERSIST. THESE CHALLENGES ARE COMPOUNDED BY LOWER EDUCATION LEVELS, HIGHER POVERTY, AND AN AGING POPULATION—ONE IN THREE RURAL OHIOANS IS OVER AGE 60. OHIO’S PLAN ALIGNS WITH FEDERAL PRIORITIES TO MAKE RURAL AMERICA HEALTHY AGAIN THROUGH SUSTAINABLE ACCESS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, INNOVATIVE CARE, AND TECH ADVANCEMENT. KEY INITIATIVES: RURAL HEALTH INNOVATION HUBS – ESTABLISH CLINICALLY INTEGRATED NETWORKS (CINS) AND REGIONAL CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE LINKING HOSPITALS, CLINICS, EMS, PHARMACISTS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO COORDINATE CARE, REDUCE COSTS, AND EXPAND CAPACITY. LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ALLOW LOW-RISK BIRTHING CENTERS IN RURAL HOSPITALS. EMERGENCY CARE TRANSFORMATION – SCALE A SUCCESSFUL PILOT ENABLING EMS TO PROVIDE TREAT-IN-PLACE OR ALTERNATE-DESTINATION CARE, REDUCING UNNECESSARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT USE THROUGH TRAINING, SYSTEM UPGRADES, AND IMPROVED CONNECTIVITY. SCHOOL-BASED HEALTH CENTERS – ESTABLISH CLINICS ON K–12 AND COLLEGE CAMPUSES OFFERING PRIMARY, BEHAVIORAL, DENTAL, AND TELEHEALTH SERVICES FOR STUDENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS, SERVING ALSO AS RURAL CLINICAL TRAINING SITES. OH SEE – EXPAND STATEWIDE MOBILE VISION, HEARING, AND DENTAL CARE BASED ON A 13-COUNTY PILOT TO ENSURE EARLY DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN. RURAL WORKFORCE PIPELINE – BUILD A CONTINUUM FROM HIGH SCHOOL THROUGH PROFESSIONAL TRAINING AND EMPLOYMENT, FEATURING UPSKILLING FOR COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS AND PHARMACISTS, FIVE-YEAR RURAL SERVICE COMMITMENTS, AND PARTNERSHIPS AMONG SCHOOLS, UNIVERSITIES, AND EMPLOYERS. CROSS-CUTTING STRATEGIES: RHTP EMBEDS TELEHEALTH, REMOTE MONITORING, AND INTEROPERABLE ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS ACROSS INITIATIVES. POLICY ACTIONS INCLUDE EXPANDING PHARMACIST SCOPE OF PRACTICE, ESTABLISHING RURAL BIRTHING CENTERS, REINSTATING THE PRESIDENTIAL FITNESS TEST, AND REQUIRING PHYSICIAN NUTRITION CME. MORE THAN 300 PARTNERS (HOSPITALS, FQHCS, UNIVERSITIES, EMS, ASSOCIATIONS) COLLABORATED ON THE PLAN. IMPLEMENTATION WILL OCCUR THROUGH LOCAL PARTNERS WITH STATE OVERSIGHT. SUSTAINABILITY: EACH PROJECT IS DESIGNED FOR LONG-TERM VIABILITY THROUGH BILLABLE SERVICE MODELS, SHARED-SERVICE EFFICIENCIES, AND ALIGNMENT WITH MEDICAID AND VALUE-BASED PAYMENT SYSTEMS. WORKFORCE INCENTIVES, TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION, AND LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ENSURE CONTINUITY BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD. EXPECTED OUTCOMES BY 2031: • ESTABLISH REGIONAL INTEGRATED NETWORKS ACROSS ALL RURAL COUNTIES. EXPANDED RURAL SBHCS. • REDUCE AVOIDABLE EMERGENCY VISITS THROUGH EMS INNOVATION. • IMPROVE DIABETES AND HYPERTENSION OUTCOMES STATEWIDE. • INCREASE THE RURAL HEALTH WORKFORCE BY AT LEAST 20%. • STRENGTHEN MATERNAL, BEHAVIORAL, AND PREVENTIVE CARE ACCESS. CONCLUSION: THIS REPRESENTS A BOLD, DATA-DRIVEN TRANSFORMATION OF RURAL HEALTHCARE IN OHIO. THROUGH TECHNOLOGY, POLICY INNOVATION, AND CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION, THE PROGRAM WILL CREATE A SUSTAINABLE MODEL THAT IMPROVES CARE QUALITY, STRENGTHENS THE WORKFORCE, AND ENHANCES HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR RURAL OHIOANS.

subaward_description: THIS PROJECT BUILDS UPON EXISTING HEALTH CENTER PROGRAM INFRASTRUCTURE IN NYE COUNTY TO EXPAND THE RANGE AND SCOPE OF PREVENTATIVE CARE SERVICES AVAILABLE IN THE COUNTY'S RURAL COMMUNITIES. SAFE HARBOR MEDICAL (SHM) IS A FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTER LOOK-ALIKE THAT SERVES SOUTHERN NEVADA AT ITS FULL-SERVICE MEDICAL CENTER IN NYE COUNTY OFFERING PRIMARY CARE, CHIROPRACTIC CARE, WOMEN'S HEALTH, PEDIATRICS, SCHOOL-BASED HEALTH SERVICES, FUNCTIONAL MEDICINE, MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT, NUTRITION COUNSELING, INSURANCE ENROLLMENT ASSISTANCE, AND WRAPAROUND CARE. OPENED IN 2025, THE SITE IN RURAL PAHRUMP PARTNERS WITH NYE COUNTY SCHOOLS TO PROVIDE BACK-TO-SCHOOL PHYSICALS AND IMMUNIZATIONS AT LOW- OR NO-COST, HELPING EXPAND ACCESS TO CARE FOR FAMILIES FACING FINANCIAL AND SOCIAL BARRIERS. SHM ALSO PARTNERS WITH NYE COUNTY JAIL TO OFFER REENTRY SERVICES COORDINATING MEDICAL CARE WITH SUPPORTIVE SERVICES FOR INDIVIDUALS WHO ARE REENTERING THE COMMUNITY POST-INCARCERATION. THE PROJECT INCLUDES TWO NECESSARY AREAS OF FOCUS: (1) SHM WILL CREATE NEW HEALTH CENTER ACCESS POINTS BY MOBILIZING A COMBINED MEDICAL/DENTAL MOBILE UNIT TO REACH RURAL AND FRONTIER COMMUNITIES, AND (2) SHM WILL ADVANCE THE LEVEL OF COMPREHENSIVE CARE AVAILABLE BY ADDING THE CAPACITY TO PROVIDE OCULAR SCREENINGS, RADIOLOGY SERVICES, PRENATAL CARE, AND DENTAL SERVICES. IT ALSO BUILDS UPON EXISTING COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS WITH SERVICE PROVIDERS WHO ARE ALREADY EMBEDDED IN THE TARGET RURAL COMMUNITIES. THROUGH ITS PARTNERS' SITES AND LOCAL COMMUNITY NETWORKS, SHM WILL BE ABLE TO PROVIDE A REGULAR SCHEDULE OF PRIMARY CARE AND DENTAL SERVICES THROUGH THE MOBILE UNIT IN COMMUNITIES THAT DO NOT CURRENTLY HAVE ACCESS TO DENTAL CARE PROVIDERS AND/OR HAVE LIMITED ACCESS TO PRIMARY AND PREVENTATIVE CARE SHM WILL INVEST IN MEDICAL TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE IN THE COMMUNITY FOR EARLY DIAGNOSIS OF CHRONIC AND ACUTE CONDITIONS THROUGH INFRASTRUCTURAL INVESTMENTS IN THE LEVEL OF CARE OFFERED THROUGH ITS NYE COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER, LOCATED IN PAHRUMP (I.E. THE ADDITION OF DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY, PRENATAL CARE, AND OCULAR SCREENING CAPABILITIES FOR UNDERINSURED/UNINSURED COMMUNITIES). PARTNERS IN THE PROGRAM INCLUDE NYE COUNTY SCHOOLS, TONOPAH CONVENTION CENTER, BEATTY COMMUNITY CENTER, GABBS FIRE SERVICES, AND MANHATTAN FIRE SERVICES, ALL OF WHICH HAVE EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH SHM AND HAVE EXPRESSED INTENT TO SUPPORT CARE EXPANSION ACROSS RURAL NYE COUNTY THROUGH THE ADDITION OF A NEW MOBILE HEALTH UNIT. THE PROGRAM WILL ACHIEVE TWO KEY EXPANSIONS IN NYE COUNTY RURAL HEALTH: (1) THE PROJECT WILL MOBILIZE ON COMBINED MEDICAL/DENTAL MOBILE HEALTH UNIT TO SERVE RURAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS NYE COUNTY WHICH CURRENTLY LACK ACCESS TO BOTH SERVICE LINES, AND (2) THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND THE RANGE OF HEALTH SERVICES AVAILABLE TO THE COMMUNITIES SERVED BY FQHCS (E.G. UNINSURED, UNDERINSURED, LOW-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS) BY EQUIPPING SHM TO PROVIDE PRENATAL CARE, DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY, AND OCULAR SCREENING SERVICES THROUGH ITS NYE COUNTY HEALTH CENTER SITE. SHM EXPECTS TO PROVIDE AT LEAST 500 PATIENT VISTS WITH THE MOBILE HEALTH UNIT PURCHASED FOR THIS PROJECT.

NORTHERN NYE COUNTY HOSPITAL DISTRICT (NNCHD) WILL EXPAND AND STRENGTHEN EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES THROUGHOUT NORTHERN NYE COUNTY BY ESTABLISHING A PROFESSIONALLY STAFFED, 24/7 EMS RESPONSE MODEL SERVING TONOPAH, ROUND MOUNTAIN, AND SURROUNDING RURAL AND FRONTIER COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES SIGNIFICANT GAPS IN EMERGENCY RESPONSE CAPACITY CAUSED BY THE REGION’S VAST GEOGRAPHY, LONG TRANSPORT DISTANCES, LIMITED LOCAL HEALTHCARE INFRASTRUCTURE, AGING AMBULANCE RESOURCES, AND HISTORIC RELIANCE ON A SMALL VOLUNTEER EMS WORKFORCE. NORTHERN NYE COUNTY ENCOMPASSES APPROXIMATELY 11,685 SQUARE MILES AND HAS FEWER THAN 6,000 RESIDENTS. THE REGION HAS NO LOCAL HOSPITAL OR EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, AND PATIENTS REQUIRING HOSPITAL-LEVEL CARE MUST GENERALLY BE TRANSPORTED MORE THAN ONE HOUR, WITH TRAUMA-LEVEL CARE REQUIRING TRAVEL OF MORE THAN TWO HOURS ONE WAY. AMBULANCE TRANSPORTS CAN REMOVE A UNIT FROM LOCAL SERVICE FOR AS LONG AS SIX HOURS, SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCING EMERGENCY RESPONSE CAPACITY FOR THE REMAINING SERVICE AREA. NNCHD WILL COMPETITIVELY PROCURE THE EMS PROVIDER DURING THE INITIAL TWO MONTHS OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, WITH CONTRACTED SERVICE IMPLEMENTATION AND PERSONNEL DEPLOYMENT TO FOLLOW UPON COMPLETION OF THE PROCUREMENT PROCESS. DURING THE OCTOBER 1, 2026 THROUGH AUGUST 30, 2027 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE, NNCHD WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EMS PROVIDER TO ESTABLISH CONTINUOUS PROFESSIONAL AMBULANCE STAFFING IN BOTH TONOPAH AND ROUND MOUNTAIN. TWO AMBULANCE UNITS WILL BE STAFFED 24 HOURS PER DAY, SEVEN DAYS PER WEEK BY A TOTAL OF 12 EMT-LEVEL PROFESSIONALS, WITH SIX PERSONNEL SUPPORTING EACH LOCATION. PERSONNEL WILL RESPOND NOT ONLY WITHIN THEIR PRIMARY STATION AREAS BUT THROUGHOUT NORTHERN NYE COUNTY AS NEEDED. NNCHD WILL SUPPORT RECRUITMENT OF QUALIFIED EMS PROFESSIONALS, INCLUDING CURRENT VOLUNTEER RESPONDERS INTERESTED IN TRANSITIONING TO PAID POSITIONS, WHILE THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER WILL EMPLOY, ONBOARD, ADMINISTER, AND SUPERVISE THE WORKFORCE. EMT-LEVEL PERSONNEL WILL ALSO BE ENCOURAGED TO PURSUE ADVANCED EMT TRAINING TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF LOCALLY AVAILABLE ADVANCED PROVIDERS AND STRENGTHEN THE REGION’S LONG-TERM EMS WORKFORCE. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO ESTABLISH ONE 24/7 AEMT-LEVEL SUPERVISORY POSITION STAFFED BY THREE PROFESSIONALS. THIS POSITION WILL PROVIDE SCHEDULING AND OPERATIONAL COORDINATION, CLINICAL OVERSIGHT, PROTOCOL COMPLIANCE, PERFORMANCE MONITORING, COORDINATION WITH VOLUNTEER RESPONDERS AND REGIONAL HEALTHCARE PARTNERS, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. THE SUPERVISOR WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY OPERATIONAL CONTACT BETWEEN THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER AND NNCHD AND WILL HELP ENSURE CONSISTENT STANDARDS OF CARE ACROSS THE EXPANDED EMS SYSTEM. THE EXPANDED SERVICE WILL BUILD UPON NNCHD’S EXISTING LOCALLY FUNDED PARTNERSHIP WITH REMSA HEALTH, WHICH CURRENTLY PROVIDES ONE 24/7 PARAMEDIC-LEVEL POSITION BASED IN TONOPAH AND OPERATING A QUICK RESPONSE VEHICLE (QRV). THE PARAMEDIC/QRV PROVIDES ADVANCED EMERGENCY INTERVENTION AND CAN RESPOND EVEN WHEN AN AMBULANCE IS UNAVAILABLE BECAUSE OF A LONG-DISTANCE TRANSPORT. THE RHT-FUNDED EXPANSION WILL ADD STAFFED AMBULANCE CAPACITY AND SYSTEMWIDE SUPERVISION WHILE INTEGRATING WITH THIS EXISTING PARAMEDIC RESOURCE TO CREATE A MORE RELIABLE AND COORDINATED EMS RESPONSE SYSTEM. THE PROJECT WILL FURTHER IMPROVE EMS READINESS THROUGH THE ACQUISITION AND DEPLOYMENT OF TWO NEW TYPE I AMBULANCES, ONE ASSIGNED TO TONOPAH AND ONE TO ROUND MOUNTAIN, TOGETHER WITH UPDATED MEDICAL AND COMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT NECESSARY TO SUPPORT SAFE EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND TRANSPORT. EQUIPMENT WILL INCLUDE POWER-LOAD STRETCHERS, CARDIAC MONITORS, VENTILATORS, STAIR CHAIRS, RADIOS, IPADS, MOBILE DATA TERMINALS, MODEMS, COMPUTERS, AND RELATED EMS EQUIPMENT. THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER WILL ALSO PROVIDE THE DISPATCH, COMMUNICATIONS, LOGISTICS, DATA MANAGEMENT, QUALITY ASSURANCE, AND ADMINISTRATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE EXPANDED SYSTEM.

FOLLOWING RENOVATION, GBC WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL THE FURNITURE, APPLIANCES, FIXTURES, AND HOUSEHOLD ITEMS NEEDED TO MAKE ALL SIX UNITS FULLY FURNISHED AND READY FOR OCCUPANCY. GREAT BASIN COLLEGE WILL ALSO WORK WITH ITS HEALTHCARE AND ACADEMIC PARTNERS TO COORDINATE CLINICAL ROTATION SCHEDULES AND HOUSING NEEDS. PARTNERS INCLUDE NORTHEASTERN NEVADA REGIONAL HOSPITAL (NNRH), NEVADA HEALTH CENTERS (NVHC), THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, RENO (UNR), THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, LAS VEGAS (UNLV), NEVADA STATE UNIVERSITY (NSU), AND OTHER HEALTHCARE AND ACADEMIC PARTNERS AS OPPORTUNITIES DEVELOP. THE COMPLETED APARTMENTS WILL PRIMARILY HOUSE HEALTHCARE TRAINEES COMPLETING CLINICAL ROTATIONS IN ELKO AND SURROUNDING RURAL COMMUNITIES. WHEN SPACE IS AVAILABLE, THEY MAY ALSO PROVIDE TEMPORARY HOUSING FOR LICENSED HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS RELOCATING TO THE AREA OR TRAVELING MEDICAL STAFF. THE HEALTHCARE OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT EXTENDS BEYOND THE RENOVATION OF SIX APARTMENTS. BY PROVIDING RELIABLE HOUSING FOR HEALTHCARE TRAINEES, GBC AND ITS PARTNERS WILL REMOVE AN IDENTIFIED BARRIER TO RURAL CLINICAL PLACEMENTS AND INCREASE THE REGION’S CAPACITY TO EXPOSE FUTURE HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS TO RURAL PRACTICE. THIS INVESTMENT WILL SUPPORT A STRONGER PIPELINE OF PHYSICIANS, NURSES, ADVANCED PRACTICE PROVIDERS, AND ALLIED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITH DIRECT EXPERIENCE SERVING RURAL NEVADA. OVER TIME, INCREASING THE NUMBER OF HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS WHO TRAIN IN NORTHEASTERN NEVADA WILL SUPPORT PROVIDER RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO PRIMARY, PREVENTIVE, AND SPECIALTY HEALTHCARE SERVICES THROUGHOUT THE REGION.

LANDER COUNTY EMS WILL COMPLETE THREE COORDINATED RURAL HEALTHCARE ACCESS AND TRAINING INITIATIVES. FIRST, LCEMS WILL ESTABLISH A DURABLE LOCAL ULTRASOUND TRAINING SYSTEM BY PURCHASING ONE INTEGRATED ULTRASOUND DIAGNOSIS SIMULATOR, TWO DEDICATED TRAINING ULTRASOUND UNITS, AND THE TABLETS, ACCESSORIES, SHIPPING, AND SETUP SUPPORT NEEDED FOR RECURRING EDUCATION IN FAST, ABDOMINAL ASSESSMENT, CARDIAC VIEWS, AND FOUNDATIONAL ULTRASOUND-GUIDED VASCULAR ACCESS. ULTRASOUND BASELINE CAPACITY CONSISTS OF THREE BUTTERFLY IQ3 UNITS DEPLOYED ON AMBULANCES, VOLUNTEER INSTRUCTIONAL SUPPORT FROM BATTLE BORN AIR EVAC, NO INTEGRATED SIMULATOR, AND NO COMPLETE DEDICATED LOCAL TRAINING PLATFORM. SECOND, LCEMS WILL PROCURE AND PLACE INTO SERVICE ONE ENCLOSED, CLIMATE-CONTROLLED COMMUNITY VENUE RAPID RESPONSE UNIT WITH A CUSTOM ENCLOSED TRAILER AND READINESS PACKAGE FOR FAIRS, RODEOS, PARKS, COMMUNITY GATHERINGS, AND LOCATIONS WHERE CROWDS OR RESTRICTED MOVEMENT LIMIT FULL-SIZE AMBULANCE ACCESS. THIRD, LCEMS WILL ESTABLISH A REMOTE RECOVERY UNIT BUILT AROUND A LOWER-COST ALL-TERRAIN UTV AMBULANCE PLATFORM, REMOTE-RECOVERY EQUIPMENT PACKAGE, ENCLOSED TRAILER, AND STORAGE, TRANSPORT, CHARGING, AND EQUIPMENT-PROTECTION FEATURES. THIS UNIT WILL SUPPORT PATIENT ACCESS AND RESPONDER SAFETY IN DESERT, OFF-ROAD, AND DIFFICULT-ACCESS ENVIRONMENTS WHERE CONVENTIONAL AMBULANCES CANNOT SAFELY OR EFFICIENTLY OPERATE. THE VEHICLE BASELINE IS AN OPEN-CAB, OPEN-PATIENT-AREA SIDE-BY-SIDE THAT IS APPROXIMATELY 12 YEARS OLD.

WILLIAM BEE RIRIE HOSPITAL WILL MODERNIZE ITS CORE TECHNOLOGY INFRASTRUCTURE TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO SPECIALTY CARE, NETWORK RELIABILITY, CYBERSECURITY, CLINICAL TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION, AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY IN ITS FRONTIER SERVICE AREA. THE PROJECT WILL DEPLOY A DEDICATED TELE-ONCOLOGY CART; REPLACE AGING CAT-5/CAT-5E CABLING WITH CAT-6A INFRASTRUCTURE; REPLACE END-OF-LIFE NETWORK SWITCHES AND WIRELESS ACCESS POINTS; INSTALL UPGRADED FIREWALL AND CYBERSECURITY TECHNOLOGY; AND UPGRADE THE ONSITE SERVER TO IMPROVE CONNECTIVITY BETWEEN THE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD AND MEDICAL EQUIPMENT. THESE IMPROVEMENTS WILL PROVIDE A MORE RELIABLE AND SECURE TECHNOLOGY ENVIRONMENT, REDUCE INTERRUPTIONS TO CLINICAL SERVICES, PRESERVE TELEHEALTH CAPACITY, AND CREATE INFRASTRUCTURE CAPABLE OF SUPPORTING FUTURE HEALTHCARE TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION.
